title: Rewrite routing failure surface and optimize region mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refactor the smart routing hotpath to (1) extract a lightweight 'routing-sentinel' that centralizes failure surface handling and circuit decision logic, (2) simplify region mapping logic to avoid repeated lookups and data races, and (3) remove implicit global locks in the policy runtime. This ticket addresses long-standing tech debt that causes p99 latency spikes and noisy fallback churn under bursty traffic. The goal is to produce a minimal, well-tested replacement for the current ad-hoc fallback plumbing that can be feature-flagged and rolled out incrementally.
acceptance_criteria: Routing sentinel component implemented and exported behind a feature flag
End-to-end tests covering node failure, regional outage, and capacity drain scenarios
Observed reduction of p99 routing decision latency by >= 20% in benchmark harness vs main branch
No increase in error rate for live canary (errors <= baseline + 0.1%) during 72h canary
Telemetry emitted for every decision path with consistent span IDs so traces link to fallback reason
Migration path documented and rollback safe; canary and 100% rollout runbooks added
updates: 2026-02-12: Triage complete. Spike planned to measure cost of extracting failure logic; identified hotspots in RegionMapper.lookup() and PolicyRuntime.evaluate().

2026-02-18: Spike results: Route decision p99 dominated by lock contention when many requests hit missing-prefetch path. Bench harness (local k8s) shows 28% CPU wasted spinning on global mutex under 5000 rps synthetic workload.

2026-02-22: Design doc uploaded with proposed 'routing-sentinel' API (conservative interface: decide(routeContext) -> Decision{target, fallback_reason, trace_id}). Linked to Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Smart+Routing+Sentinel
2026-02-25: Implementation started. Extracted RegionMapper cache and added ReadMostlyMap with epoch-based invalidation to avoid coarse locks. Initial unit tests added.

2026-03-01: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2981. PR includes feature flag 'routing.sentinel_v1' and integration tests in the runtests suite. Requested design/eng review from @marco and @sylvia.

2026-03-03: Code review feedback: avoid exposing internal Decision struct to public API; changed to opaque DecisionToken with reconciliation endpoint. Also, ensure sentinel does not change request prioritization semantics (preserve fairness).

2026-03-05: Canary started at 2% traffic. Observed decision latency improvement at canary hosts: median -5ms, p95 -12ms, p99 -32ms relative to baseline. No user-facing errors. Telemetry flags show reduced fallback churn for overloaded GPUs.

2026-03-08: Internal benchmarks replicated in perf lab: end-to-end routing throughput +18% for small-seq workloads with batching enabled. CPU usage on routing hosts reduced by ~22% under 10k rps synthetic tests.

2026-03-10: Added additional e2e scenario for regional flapping (simulate repeated region leases). Sentinel correctly consolidates repeated failovers and emits single aggregated fallback events. Preparing 25% canary ramp.
Notes: keep sentinel implementation intentionally small — complex heuristics will remain in policy adapters outside hotpath. Add feature-flag guard and telemetry knobs before wider rollout.
follow_up_tasks: Expand sentinel telemetry to include histogram of lease-age and queue-depth
Refactor policy adapters to use new DecisionToken reconciliation API
Add regression alerts to CI for routing latency and fallback rate
Plan Dedicated migration notes for customers pinning region-affinity
risks: Risk: subtle change in decision ordering could impact fairness for high-priority tenants. Mitigation: add synthetic fairness tests and compare traces.
Risk: feature flag path diverges from legacy sooner than expected. Mitigation: keep both codepaths compiled and add nightly end-to-end parity tests.
Risk: regional mapping cache invalidation bugs causing stale routing decisions. Mitigation: epoch-based invalidation and conservative TTLs, plus safeguard metrics.
Risk: increased complexity in debugging without linking spans; mitigation: emit consistent span IDs and include fallback reason labels
